story.head: The Panthers should pile up the shots
paras: The Panthers won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-2 in Chicago on Oct 25. The Panthers have won three straight, while the Blackhawks (4-9-0) lost 4-1 to Detroit on Thursday. Going in, the Hawks are last in the Central (31st in the NHL) and the Panthers third in the Atlantic (tied for sixth).

The Blackhawks have played better than their record (.308) says: their chances are worth about .368, and their finishing has held them back. The Panthers’ record (.643) is about what their chances are worth.

The Blackhawks do a lot of their shooting from distance (2nd lowest), don't block many shots (32nd) and have struggled on the power play (32nd). Chicago has scored 2.08 goals a game, the second fewest in the league, and allowed 3.69, the fourth most. The Panthers forecheck harder than anyone (1st) and rarely ice the puck (1st). They also are the league’s most physical team (1st), so the Panthers hit a lot, but the Blackhawks mostly don’t. The Panthers are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Blackhawks.

Patrick Kane (1 G / 7 A / 8 P in 13 GP) leads the Blackhawks in scoring, and Roman Kantserov (5 G / 1 A / 6 P in 13 GP) has a team-high five goals. Matthew Tkachuk (4 G / 16 A / 20 P in 14 GP) leads the Panthers in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, and Brady Tkachuk (8 G / 7 A / 15 P in 14 GP) has a team-high eight goals.
Spencer Knight (4-7-0 / .897 SV% in 11 GS) will likely start for Chicago, and Akira Schmid (5-2-1 / .888 SV% in 7 GS) for Florida.
The Panthers usually control more of the chances than the Blackhawks do.
